articles.title: What the Fortibleed campaign means for organizations running FortiGate firewalls
articles.summary: A sophisticated, automated credential-harvesting campaign dubbed FortiBleed has compromised thousands of FortiGate firewalls by leveraging exposed attacker tools and scripts. The operation allowed attackers to gain deep access to victim networks, including full domain-level control in some instances.

articles.title: Algerian man charged with running two cybercrime marketplaces
articles.summary: An Algerian national, Abdellah Belmili, has been charged by federal prosecutors for allegedly operating two dark-web marketplaces that sold stolen financial credentials and phishing kits targeting U.S. banks.

articles.title: GitHub Updates actions/checkout to Block Common Pwn Request Attack Patterns
articles.summary: GitHub is updating the 'actions/checkout' tool to mitigate security risks associated with 'pull_request_target' triggers, which have been exploited to execute malicious code with elevated privileges. The update aims to harden software supply chain security starting June 18, 2026.

articles.title: New N-able feature gives IT teams visibility into AI usage across endpoints and networks
articles.summary: N-able has introduced a new 'Shadow AI Visibility' feature across its UEM and security platforms to help IT teams track and manage unauthorized AI tool usage on endpoints and networks. This tool aims to mitigate security risks associated with the rapid and often unmonitored adoption of AI applications within corporate environments.

articles.title: The Exploit Doesn't Exist. You Can Still Prove It Works Against You
articles.summary: The article discusses how security teams can proactively validate vulnerability exploitability to defend against threats before public exploits are released. This approach helps organizations mitigate risk despite the speed at which attackers weaponize new vulnerabilities.

articles.title: LastPass confirms data breach in Klue supply chain attack
articles.summary: LastPass confirmed a data breach involving unauthorized access to customer data within their Salesforce environment, resulting from a supply chain attack targeting the company's OAuth tokens via Klue.

articles.title: Dragos unveils OT-native AI to help critical infrastructure teams prioritize threats faster
articles.summary: Dragos has launched EmberAI, an operational technology-native AI tool designed to help critical infrastructure teams analyze and prioritize security threats using historical and real-time intelligence. The platform aims to improve asset visibility and vulnerability management by leveraging over a decade of specialized industrial security expertise.

articles.title: Using Reddit to manipulate AI search results is surprisingly easy
articles.summary: A Cornell Tech study reveals that AI research agents can be easily manipulated by brief, targeted Reddit comments, raising significant concerns about the integrity of AI-generated reports. This vulnerability highlights the risks of AI systems relying on unverified, community-generated content from the web.

articles.title: Two Scattered Spider members plead guilty over cyberattack that crippled London transit
articles.summary: Two members of the threat group Scattered Spider have pleaded guilty to infiltrating Transport for London's network, which caused significant and long-term disruption to public transit services in 2024.

articles.title: Webinar: Why email security teams are drowning in alerts
articles.summary: The headline highlights the issue of alert fatigue in email security teams caused by the high volume of phishing and account takeover attacks. It suggests that leveraging behavioral AI for automation can improve operational efficiency and response times.

articles.title: New CryptoBandits Malware Uses USB Drives and Tor to Steal Crypto
articles.summary: Microsoft researchers have identified 'CryptoBandits,' a new malware strain that leverages USB drives and the Tor network to hijack cryptocurrency transactions by modifying wallet addresses. This dual-action clipper poses a significant risk to cryptocurrency users by redirecting funds during transfer processes.

articles.title: Agentic AI: The Weapon That No Longer Needs a Warrior
articles.summary: The rise of agentic AI represents a paradigm shift where autonomous systems can select and engage targets without direct human intervention. This evolution fundamentally alters the nature of cyber warfare by removing the human decision-maker from the loop.

articles.title: The Evolution of iGaming Fraud: What Security Teams Should Expect in 2027
articles.summary: This article explores how emerging technologies like AI, deepfakes, and fraud-as-a-service are expected to evolve the iGaming threat landscape by 2027. It provides actionable guidance for security teams to prepare their defenses against these sophisticated future risks.

articles.title: GTA 6 early access offers are taking gamers’ crypto
articles.summary: Scammers are setting up fraudulent websites promising early access to GTA 6 in exchange for cryptocurrency payments to deceive eager gamers. These sites are unauthorized and provide no access to the game, resulting in financial loss for victims.

articles.title: Xsolis Data Breach Impacts 1.4 Million People
articles.summary: Healthcare technology firm Xsolis suffered a data breach caused by a phishing attack, exposing the personal and medical information of 1.4 million individuals. The incident compromised sensitive data from the company's hospital client systems.

articles.title: 2 Scattered Spider-Linked Hackers Plead Guilty Over £39M TfL Cyberattack
articles.summary: Two teenagers associated with the Scattered Spider group have pleaded guilty to orchestrating a major cyberattack against Transport for London and various US healthcare organizations, resulting in millions of pounds of damages. The individuals are currently awaiting sentencing for their roles in the breaches.

articles.title: Two Scattered Spider hackers plead guilty over Transport for London cyberattack
articles.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider hacker group have pleaded guilty to charges linked to a 2024 cyberattack on Transport for London that incurred £29 million in costs. The defendants face sentencing in July for their violations of the UK's Computer Misuse Act.

articles.title: Omada Identity Sovereign targets Europe’s growing digital sovereignty demands
articles.summary: Omada has launched Omada Identity Sovereign to help regulated European organizations meet strict digital sovereignty and compliance requirements for identity governance. The solution is designed to align with evolving regulatory frameworks like DORA and NIS2.

articles.title: Hack The Box adds crisis simulations and SOC training to strengthen cyber readiness
articles.summary: Hack The Box has expanded its platform with new SOC training, crisis simulations, and AI-driven tools to help organizations improve cybersecurity team readiness and operational resilience. These additions aim to help security leaders identify skill gaps and better prepare for evolving AI-based cyber threats.

articles.title: Mavenir turns NOC knowledge into automation for autonomous networks
articles.summary: Mavenir has launched an Agentic Service Assurance Framework designed to automate complex network operations across 5G and cloud-native environments using a multi-agent AI system. The platform aims to streamline fault detection and resolution without requiring the replacement of existing infrastructure.

articles.title: Malicious npm Packages Pose as PostCSS Tools to Deliver Windows RAT
articles.summary: Researchers discovered malicious npm packages masquerading as PostCSS tools to infect Windows systems with a remote access trojan. The packages were recently published and have recorded several hundred downloads.

articles.title: OpenAI wants AI to fix vulnerabilities, not just find them
articles.summary: OpenAI has expanded its Daybreak initiative to integrate AI models and security tools designed to not only identify software vulnerabilities but also facilitate their automated remediation. This effort aims to alleviate industry pressure by streamlining the patching process for developers and security teams.

articles.title: F5 launches AI Security Platform to uncover and secure shadow AI
articles.summary: F5 has launched an AI Security Platform to provide visibility and governance for enterprise AI deployments, bolstered by the acquisition of SurePath AI. The platform aims to mitigate risks associated with shadow AI by continuously monitoring and protecting AI models, agents, and their connecting APIs.

articles.title: Phishing hides in routine Microsoft 365 workflows
articles.summary: Attackers are exploiting Microsoft 365 collaboration tools and Outlook Groups to disguise phishing attempts as routine, trusted productivity workflows. This technique bypasses traditional security filters by embedding malicious actions within legitimate-looking notifications.

articles.title: ShapedPlugin Supply Chain Attack Backdoors Pro Plugin Updates
articles.summary: Attackers compromised the software supply chain of ShapedPlugin to inject backdoors into plugin updates, allowing for credential theft and unauthorized site access. Users who updated these plugins between April and June 2026 are at risk of a full system compromise.

articles.title: Squidbleed: 29-Year-Old Squid Bug Leaks User Credentials
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a long-standing memory leak vulnerability in Squid Proxy, dubbed Squidbleed, that has existed since 1997 and allows for the exposure of sensitive user credentials and HTTP data. The flaw is identified as CVE-2026-47729.

articles.title: WhatsApp VBScript Campaign Uses Fake Documents to Install ManageEngine RMM Tool
articles.summary: Attackers are distributing malicious VBScript files via WhatsApp Desktop and Web to install legitimate ManageEngine RMM software, enabling unauthorized remote access. The campaign is currently targeting users across multiple global regions.

articles.title: A $1,400 experiment in AI security auditing outperformed OpenAI’s Codex Security
articles.summary: Researchers developed EVOHUNT, a system that utilizes an optimized external playbook to enable AI agents to identify software vulnerabilities more effectively than OpenAI’s commercial Codex model at a significantly lower cost. This highlights the potential for cost-effective, specialized open-source AI tools in automated security auditing.

articles.title: Five Eyes spooks warn AI means infosec incidents can become ‘major operational and financial crises’
articles.summary: The Five Eyes intelligence alliance has warned that AI-driven cyber threats are escalating, potentially transforming routine security incidents into severe operational and financial crises. Executives are urged to prioritize robust cybersecurity measures to mitigate these emerging risks.

articles.title: OpenAI Expands Daybreak With GPT-5.5-Cyber to Help Defenders Patch Security Flaws
articles.summary: OpenAI has launched an enhanced version of its GPT-5.5-Cyber model as part of the Daybreak initiative to assist cybersecurity defenders in identifying and patching complex software vulnerabilities. This tool is designed to perform deep code analysis to help secure large codebases.

articles.title: Sniff out stale AI override advice with this open source CLI
articles.summary: A new open-source CLI tool has been released to help developers identify and remediate stale AI override advice and insecure package dependencies. The tool focuses on mitigating vulnerabilities that are often difficult to detect within software supply chains.

articles.title: OpenAI: Yoo-hoo, look over here, we do that security stuff too!
articles.summary: OpenAI has announced new security initiatives, including a 'Patch The Planet' pledge, aimed at strengthening their vulnerability management and cybersecurity posture. This move highlights the company's commitment to proactive security measures as part of their broader development strategy.

articles.title: WhatsApp phishing attack uses fake business docs to hack PCs
articles.summary: A sophisticated malware campaign is targeting WhatsApp users by sending deceptive messages containing malicious VBScript files disguised as business documents. Once executed, these files grant attackers unauthorized remote access to the victim's computer.

articles.title: Court rules SAVE database illegal, orders it dismantled
articles.summary: A judge has ordered the dismantling of the government's SAVE database after ruling that its operations violated multiple federal statutes, including the Privacy Act. The court concluded that the database's data collection and usage procedures were illegal.

articles.title: The Global Namespace Risk: Universal Bucket Hijacking Technique for Cloud Data Exfiltration
articles.summary: Unit 42 researchers have identified a vulnerability where the global uniqueness of cloud storage namespaces allows attackers to perform bucket hijacking, enabling the redirection and exfiltration of data across major cloud service providers.

articles.title: JaredFromSubway MEV bot hacked in $15 million crypto theft
articles.summary: The infamous JaredFromSubway Ethereum MEV bot was exploited for $15 million after an attacker tricked its detection logic with fake trading opportunities. The incident highlights the inherent risks of automated high-frequency trading bots in the decentralized finance space.

articles.title: FFmpeg fixes PixelSmash flaw in widely used video decoder
articles.summary: The PixelSmash vulnerability in the widely used FFmpeg library allows for remote code execution and denial-of-service attacks across several popular media and cloud applications. Developers have released a fix to address the flaw and mitigate potential exploitation.

articles.title: WhatsApp Malware Campaign Hijacks Trust, Installs Legitimate Admin Tools
articles.summary: Attackers are hijacking WhatsApp accounts to distribute fake debt notices that install remote access tools, granting them unauthorized control over victims' computers. The campaign is actively ongoing and relies on the deployment of legitimate administrative software to bypass security detection.

articles.title: Cloudflare teams up with big browsers to help websites tell welcome from unwelcome visitors
articles.summary: Cloudflare has collaborated with major browser developers to implement Private Access Control Tokens, a mechanism designed to differentiate between human users and malicious bots. This initiative aims to reduce automated fraud by verifying device legitimacy without compromising user privacy.

articles.title: FortiBleed campaign used custom FortiGate sniffer to steal credentials
articles.summary: The FortiBleed campaign leveraged custom sniffer tools on compromised Fortinet FortiGate firewalls to harvest authentication credentials. This large-scale operation highlights a targeted effort to compromise network infrastructure to steal sensitive access data.

articles.title: Trump executive orders speed up post-quantum migration, boost industry
articles.summary: Recent executive orders signed by Donald Trump aim to accelerate the U.S. federal government's migration to post-quantum encryption while fostering the growth of the domestic quantum computing sector.

articles.title: Security shops among the 'hundreds' of Klue hack victims
articles.summary: Hundreds of organizations using Klue have been compromised by the Icarus extortion group, which is actively exploiting vulnerabilities within Salesforce-linked integrations. The breach highlights significant supply chain risks associated with third-party software integrations.

articles.title: Texas Parks & Wildlife (TPWD) Data Breach impacts 3 Million People
articles.summary: The Texas Parks and Wildlife Department (TPWD) experienced a data breach affecting 3 million individuals after a third-party vendor used for license processing was compromised, exposing sensitive personal information.

articles.title: ShapedPlugin WordPress Pro Plugins Backdoored in Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary: ShapedPlugin's WordPress Pro plugins were compromised in a supply chain attack where attackers injected backdoor code into official release channels. This allowed malicious updates to be pushed directly to users via licensed distribution paths.

articles.title: Beats Studio Buds Flaw Could Let Nearby Attackers Eavesdrop on Users
articles.summary: Apple has issued a security patch for a vulnerability in Beats Studio Buds that allowed nearby attackers to intercept microphone audio. The update addresses a significant privacy flaw affecting device users.

articles.title: Microsoft says Windows 11 26H2 is coming soon, details upgrade process
articles.summary: Microsoft has announced that Windows 11 26H2 is the upcoming feature update, which will be deployable for users on versions 24H2 and 25H2 via a lightweight enablement package.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes AutoGen Studio flaw that enabled code execution
articles.summary: Microsoft has patched a vulnerability chain called AutoJack in its AutoGen Studio interface that allowed attackers to execute arbitrary code on a host system through a malicious webpage. The flaw specifically targeted the prototyping tool for AI agents.

articles.title: Researchers Detail DifyTap Flaws in Dify That Could Expose AI Chats Across Tenants
articles.summary: Researchers identified four unauthenticated vulnerabilities in the Dify AI platform, collectively dubbed DifyTap, that allow unauthorized access to AI chat data across different tenants. These flaws pose a significant risk to data privacy for users of the open-source agentic workflow platform.

articles.title: Intel agencies: Frontier AI models will reshape cybersecurity faster than expected
articles.summary: Intelligence agencies from the Five Eyes alliance have issued a joint warning that frontier AI models are accelerating changes to the cybersecurity landscape more rapidly than previously anticipated. This advisory underscores growing global concerns regarding the dual-use nature of advanced artificial intelligence technologies.

articles.title: Texas Parks and Wildlife Data Breach Affects Over 3M License Customers
articles.summary: A third-party vendor breach has exposed the sensitive personal data, including driver's license and passport numbers, of approximately 3 million Texas Parks and Wildlife customers.

articles.title: 29-Year-Old Squid Proxy Bug 'Squidbleed' Can Leak Cleartext HTTP Requests
articles.summary: A 29-year-old heap over-read vulnerability dubbed 'Squidbleed' allows local attackers to intercept cleartext HTTP requests, including sensitive credentials, from other users on the same Squid proxy. The flaw, originating from a 1997 code change, remains present in default configurations.

articles.title: Canadian utility fesses up to data breach, but key details remain off-grid
articles.summary: London Hydro has confirmed a data breach potentially compromising customer names, addresses, and account details, though specific details regarding the incident remain undisclosed. The utility company is currently investigating the scope and nature of the intrusion.

articles.title: Threat Hunting Beyond Alerts: Finding the Activity Detection Misses
articles.summary: This article explores proactive threat hunting strategies designed to uncover malicious activity that automated security alerts and traditional detection systems often fail to identify.

articles.title: Suspected cyberattack triggers false emergency alerts across parts of Brazil
articles.summary: Unauthorized actors compromised Brazil's Civil Defense Alert system, resulting in the dissemination of false emergency notifications to the public. The incident highlights a security breach within a critical national infrastructure platform.

articles.title: A Glimpse into the “Search Your Target” Market for Stolen Credentials
articles.summary: The emergence of an underground market allows attackers to outsource the time-consuming process of searching large credential dumps for specific target data. This service lowers the barrier to entry for cybercriminals looking to acquire actionable intelligence on specific organizations.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Mythos AI broke into almost all NSA classified systems in hours
articles.summary: The Trump administration has ordered Anthropic to restrict access to its most powerful AI models, Mythos 5 and Fable 5, to U.S. citizens following allegations that the systems successfully breached NSA and Cyber Command networks. The move highlights the challenges of enforcing strict nationality-based access controls on rapidly evolving AI technologies.

articles.title: New OXLOADER Loader Uses Malicious Google Ads to Deliver CastleStealer
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a new malware loader called OXLOADER that uses malicious Google Ads to distribute the CastleStealer infostealer. The campaign is attributed to a likely Russian-speaking, financially motivated threat actor.

articles.title: Brazil probes emergency warning system after nationwide rogue alert
articles.summary: Brazilian authorities are investigating a security failure in the national emergency warning system that caused devices across the country to display the unauthorized word 'misanthropy'. The incident highlights a potential vulnerability in the country's public alert infrastructure.

articles.title: Scammers Use Fake GitHub Stars, VirusTotal Reviews to Spread Crypto Clipper
articles.summary: Cybercriminals are distributing a multi-platform crypto clipper malware by manipulating social proof metrics like fake GitHub stars and VirusTotal reviews to deceive Windows and Mac users. The malicious campaign embeds over 15,000 attacker-controlled wallets to facilitate the theft of cryptocurrency.

articles.title: Google Sets Sept. 30 Deadline for Android Developer Verification in Four Countries
articles.summary: Google will begin enforcing mandatory developer identity verification for Android apps in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand starting September 30, 2026. Apps from unverified developers will be blocked from installation on certified devices in these regions.

articles.title: Stop Your Legacy Infrastructure from Hijacking Your AI Agents
articles.summary: Security researchers are warning that attackers are bypassing modern AI security protocols by exploiting vulnerabilities within outdated legacy infrastructure. This emerging attack vector allows threat actors to hijack AI agents, highlighting a critical gap in current organizational security programs.

articles.title: Health board apologizes for phishing staff with with bogus vacation day
articles.summary: A Canadian health board issued an apology after conducting a phishing simulation that used a fake offer of extra vacation time to test employees. The incident drew criticism for exploiting the stress of medical workers during a sensitive period.

articles.title: Salesforce Disables Klue Integration After OAuth Token Theft Hits Customer Data
articles.summary: The Icarus extortion group exploited a legacy Klue credential to perform an OAuth token theft, resulting in unauthorized access to Salesforce data. In response, Salesforce has disabled the Klue integration to prevent further exfiltration.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Browser Bugs, EDR Killers, TV Botnet, OpenBSD Flaw, Android Trojan, and More
articles.summary: This weekly recap highlights a persistent landscape of cyber threats, including browser exploits, EDR evasion techniques, and mobile malware targeting users through deceptive downloads and weak security hygiene.

articles.title: FortiBleed: The Most Detailed Breakdown Yet of an Active Russian Credential-Harvesting Operation
articles.summary: The FortiBleed campaign has compromised over 430,000 FortiGate devices to harvest 110 million credentials, marking a major, ongoing Russian-linked cyber espionage operation. A comprehensive report from SOCRadar provides new technical insights into the scale and impact of this widespread credential-harvesting activity.

articles.title: Gizmodo readers hit with ClickFix malware prompts after account compromise
articles.summary: Gizmodo readers were targeted by a ClickFix malware campaign following a website account compromise that prompted Windows users to run malicious files. While Windows systems were at high risk, Mac users appeared to be unaffected by the specific payload.

articles.title: Canada’s Spy Agency Used First-of-Its-Kind Warrant to Clean Botnet-Infected Devices
articles.summary: The Canadian Security Intelligence Service successfully obtained a judicial warrant to remotely neutralize foreign-run botnets by modifying infected local servers, routers, and IoT devices. This marks the first time the agency has utilized threat reduction powers to directly intervene in compromised civilian infrastructure.

articles.title: 4,300+ Outdated Routers Hijacked in Stealthy Spy Infrastructure by AryStinger malware
articles.summary: The AryStinger malware has compromised over 4,300 outdated routers by exploiting long-standing vulnerabilities to establish a stealthy infrastructure for reconnaissance and cyber-espionage. Security researchers identified the campaign after tracking a binary spreading through flaws dating back to 2013 and 2016.

articles.title: 23 ClawHub plugins squatting official scopes expose AI registry security gaps
articles.summary: Twenty-three malicious plugins were discovered using official 'ClawHub' and 'OpenClaw' scopes to execute unauthorized code, highlighting significant security vulnerabilities in AI agent plugin registries. The incident underscores a lack of scope reservation controls that allows attackers to impersonate official publishers.

articles.title: usbliter8 Brings Unpatchable BootROM Exploit to Apple A12 and A13 Devices
articles.summary: Security researchers have released usbliter8, an unpatchable BootROM exploit targeting Apple's A12 and A13 chips that enables arbitrary code execution within the SecureROM. This vulnerability extends critical security risks similar to the checkm8 exploit to a wider range of newer iPhone devices.

articles.title: AryStinger Malware Infects 4,300 Legacy Routers to Build Reconnaissance Proxy Network
articles.summary: A new malware family called AryStinger has compromised over 4,300 legacy routers to establish a distributed reconnaissance and proxy network for pre-attack staging. Unlike typical router botnets, this strain focuses on stealthy network intelligence rather than DDoS operations.

articles.title: INTERPOL Warns Phishing, Ransomware, and AI Scams Are Rising Across Asia-Pacific
articles.summary: INTERPOL's latest report identifies a significant surge in cybercrime across the Asia-Pacific region, driven by rapid digital transformation and the exploitation of emerging technologies like AI. Phishing, ransomware, and AI-enabled scams are highlighted as the primary threats facing the area.

articles.title: Who pays when you gate cyber-capable AI models?
articles.summary: Jaya Baloo discusses the debate over restricting access to cyber-capable AI models, arguing that policymakers fail to consider how such gates may disadvantage security teams and widen the capability gap between attackers and defenders.

articles.title: Agent Beacon: Open-source telemetry layer for AI agents
articles.summary: Agent Beacon is a new open-source telemetry tool designed to monitor and normalize activity logs for AI coding agents running across local, CI, and cloud environments. It aims to improve visibility into the actions, commands, and tool calls executed by AI development agents.

articles.title: Encrypted DNS still tells an eavesdropper where to look
articles.summary: While encrypted DNS protocols protect the contents of queries, researchers highlight that plaintext packet headers still expose user browsing habits to network eavesdroppers. The study specifically evaluates this information leakage within Internet of Things (IoT) environments.

articles.title: Product showcase: Avira Security for iOS blends security, privacy, and device optimization
articles.summary: Avira has released an updated security application for iOS that integrates privacy, security, and device optimization tools into a single platform. The app is designed to improve user experience through a streamlined onboarding process and customizable privacy settings.

articles.title: Hundreds of AI-powered iOS apps found exposing credentials
articles.summary: Researchers at Wake Forest University discovered that 282 out of 444 analyzed iOS apps with AI features leaked exploitable LLM API credentials through network traffic. This vulnerability exposes backend access mechanisms across numerous application categories.

articles.title: The systemd 261 release brings a software TPM, new OS installer
articles.summary: The release of systemd 261 introduces new features including a software TPM, an OS installer, and a cloud metadata subsystem (systemd-imdsd). These updates aim to enhance cloud instance management and system initialization capabilities for Linux distributions.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 102
articles.summary: The Security Affairs Malware Newsletter summarizes recent cyber threats, including a major supply chain attack on OptinMonster affecting 1.2 million sites and ongoing espionage campaigns by China-nexus actors targeting research sectors.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 582 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: The 582nd edition of the Security Affairs newsletter features analysis on the GentleKiller EDR-killer, a Fortinet credential-spraying campaign, and active CISA warnings. It serves as a weekly digest of significant cybersecurity developments and threat intelligence.

articles.title: AryStinger botnet infected thousands of D-Link routers worldwide
articles.summary: The newly discovered AryStinger botnet has compromised over 4,000 outdated D-Link routers, repurposing them as proxies for malicious traffic. These devices are being exploited due to their lack of current security patches.

articles.title: Week in review: 74k Fortinet firewall credentials stolen, Splunk Enterprise RCE under active attack
articles.summary: Recent cybersecurity news highlights the theft of 74,000 Fortinet firewall credentials, active exploitation of a Splunk Enterprise RCE vulnerability, and the discovery of a hardware-level backdoor attack named HAMLOCK.

articles.title: Inside GentleKiller: The EDR-Killer Powering The Gentlemen
articles.summary: The cybercriminal group 'The Gentlemen' is utilizing a sophisticated EDR-killing tool called 'GentleKiller' that leverages BYOVD exploits to disable security software before deploying ransomware. This technical infrastructure was detailed in an ESET investigation following a significant internal data leak.

articles.title: Inside GentleKiller: The EDR-Killer Powering The Gentlemen
articles.summary: The cybercrime group known as The Gentlemen is utilizing a sophisticated EDR-killer tool called GentleKiller to neutralize security software via BYOVD exploits prior to launching ransomware attacks. ESET researchers recently detailed the group's infrastructure, which was further confirmed by internal data leaks.

articles.title: New Prinz Eugen ransomware prioritizes recent files for encryption
articles.summary: The Prinz Eugen ransomware is a newly identified operation that targets recently modified files for encryption while notably omitting ransom notes. This stealthy behavior suggests a focus on rapid data impact during active intrusions.

articles.title: Why Amazon hates 'human-in-the-loop' AI governance
articles.summary: Amazon VP Eric Brandwine argues that human-in-the-loop AI governance is inefficient because human decision-making is prone to error and scalability issues. The perspective suggests a shift toward more automated oversight mechanisms within corporate AI policy.

articles.title: Microsoft links Mastra AI supply chain attack to North Korean hackers
articles.summary: Microsoft has attributed a supply chain attack involving over 140 compromised npm packages to the North Korean state-sponsored threat group Sapphire Sleet. The incident highlights the ongoing risk of malicious software packages being used for unauthorized system access.

articles.title: MDR Provider Comparison: Time to Discover and Respond to Threats
articles.summary: This guide provides a comprehensive comparison of Managed Detection and Response (MDR) providers, focusing on key performance metrics like response speed and threat intelligence capabilities to assist organizations in vendor selection.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin Bug to Expose API Keys
articles.summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a medium-severity vulnerability in the Gravity SMTP WordPress plugin to extract sensitive information, including API keys and OAuth tokens. Users are advised to update their installations to mitigate the risk of data exposure.

articles.title: FortiBleed Exposes Global Credential-Spraying Operation
articles.summary: A massive industrial-scale credential-spraying campaign targeted global Fortinet VPN devices, resulting in widespread organizational compromises. The attack was discovered by security researcher Volodymyr Diachenko due to the threat actors' operational negligence.

articles.title: CISA Warns of Active Exploitation Following FortiBleed Leak
articles.summary: CISA has issued an emergency alert following the leak of credentials for approximately 74,000 Fortinet devices, which are currently being actively exploited by threat actors. This security incident, dubbed 'FortiBleed,' affects various firewalls and VPN gateways worldwide.

articles.title: Threat Brief: Mitigating Large-Scale Credential Attacks
articles.summary: Unit 42 provides strategic guidance for defending against large-scale credential stuffing attacks, specifically addressing recent campaigns that target security vendor infrastructure.

articles.title: Klue OAuth breach victim list grows as Icarus hackers claim attack
articles.summary: Market intelligence platform Klue confirmed a security incident involving the theft of OAuth tokens connected to customer Salesforce environments, with the Icarus extortion group claiming responsibility. The breach has led to an expanding list of affected organizations.

articles.title: Hackers exploit info disclosure bug in Gravity SMTP WordPress plugin
articles.summary: Hackers are actively exploiting an unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability within the Gravity SMTP WordPress plugin, which is installed on over 100,000 websites.

articles.title: Unpatchable 'usbliter8' Exploit Breaks Apple A12 and A13 SecureROM Boot Chain
articles.summary: Security researchers have discovered an unpatchable exploit called 'usbliter8' affecting the SecureROM of Apple's A12 and A13 chips, allowing for arbitrary code execution. Because the vulnerability is tied to the hardware, it cannot be mitigated via software updates.

articles.title: The Gentlemen RaaS Uses GentleKiller EDR Framework Targeting 400 Security Processes
articles.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) group is distributing a sophisticated framework called GentleKiller, which enables affiliates to terminate over 400 security processes to bypass endpoint detection. This development highlights the growing trend of threat actors utilizing specialized EDR-killing tools to facilitate ransomware deployment.

articles.title: Meteor 3.0 Migration Helped Rocket.Chat Move Off End-of-Life Node.js Runtime
articles.summary: Rocket.Chat migrated to Meteor 3.0 to upgrade its underlying Node.js runtime from version 14 to 20. This update effectively resolves technical debt associated with the removal of Fibers and mitigates supply-chain security risks for federal users.

articles.title: Texas govt data breach exposes over 3 million driver’s licenses
articles.summary: The Texas Parks and Wildlife Department suffered a data breach involving a third-party vendor, resulting in the exposure of personal information for over three million driver's license holders. The incident highlights the risks associated with supply chain security for government entities.

articles.title: Researchers drop checkm8-style BootROM exploit for A12 and A13 iPhones
articles.summary: Security researchers have released a permanent, unpatchable BootROM exploit affecting A12 and A13 chipsets in certain iPhone models. Because the flaw exists at the hardware level, it cannot be fixed via software updates.

articles.title: AutoJack Attack Lets One Web Page Hijack AI Agent for Host Code Execution
articles.summary: Microsoft researchers discovered AutoJack, a vulnerability that allows malicious web pages to exploit AI browsing agents to execute arbitrary code on a host machine. The attack bypasses authentication and requires no user interaction after the initial page load.

articles.title: Operation Endgame Disrupts SocGholish Servers, Cleans 14,971 WordPress Sites
articles.summary: International law enforcement agencies collaborated in Operation Endgame to dismantle SocGholish malicious infrastructure, resulting in the cleanup of nearly 15,000 compromised WordPress websites.

articles.title: Gcore Helps Ucom Safeguard Public Live Broadcast Infrastructure During Armenia’s Parliamentary Elections
articles.summary: Gcore provided infrastructure protection services to Ucom to secure public live broadcasting during Armenia's parliamentary elections. The collaboration focused on safeguarding critical communications against potential cyber disruptions during a sensitive political event.

articles.title: CISA Warns Fortinet Customers as FortiBleed Hits 86,644 FortiGate Devices
articles.summary: CISA has issued an urgent warning to Fortinet customers regarding the 'FortiBleed' campaign, which has compromised over 86,000 internet-accessible FortiGate devices. The campaign is attributed to Russian-speaking threat actors, prompting authorities to advise immediate patching and security measures.

articles.title: Nintendo America Employee Data Exposed After Shadowbyt3$ Targets TinyPulse
articles.summary: The hacker group Shadowbyt3 breached the employee engagement platform TinyPulse, resulting in the exposure of sensitive HR and financial records belonging to Nintendo of America staff. The compromised data includes tax forms, banking details, and internal survey responses.

articles.title: 14,971 WordPress Sites Cleaned in Global SocGholish Takedown
articles.summary: Law enforcement agencies from four countries conducted Operation EndGame, successfully dismantling the SocGholish malware infrastructure and cleaning nearly 15,000 infected WordPress sites.

articles.title: eFAQ Publishes Investigation Into Alleged Scam Activity and Coordinated Reputation Attacks
articles.summary: eFAQ has released an investigative report detailing allegations of scam operations and orchestrated campaigns designed to damage reputations. The report highlights the impact of coordinated disinformation efforts on digital trust.

articles.title: Every AI Agent Is an Identity. Most Organizations Don't Treat Them That Way
articles.summary: AI agents now possess significant operational capabilities within corporate environments, yet they often lack the robust identity management and governance protocols required to secure them. This creates a critical security gap as these autonomous systems become high-value targets for attackers.

articles.title: Everything's bigger and better in Texas – even data breaches
articles.summary: A data breach involving Texas hunting and fishing licenses has exposed the personal information of approximately 3 million residents. The incident highlights a significant security failure affecting a large portion of the state's population.

articles.title: Klue breach lead to Salesforce data theft, Huntress affected
articles.summary: A security breach at market intelligence platform Klue led to the compromise of integration credentials, resulting in unauthorized access and data theft from connected services like Salesforce for companies including Huntress. The incident highlights the risks of a supply chain attack cascading through third-party integrations.

articles.title: Police raid malware network tied to Russia's Evil Corp hacker group
articles.summary: An international law enforcement operation has successfully targeted the SocGholish botnet, a malware distribution network associated with the Russian-based cybercrime organization Evil Corp.

articles.title: Webinar: How attackers bypass MFA and how defenders can respond
articles.summary: This webinar examines how modern phishing techniques like Device Code attacks bypass MFA and discusses using behavioral AI to detect and automate responses to compromised accounts.

articles.title: Cybercriminals abused GitHub, YouTube and VirusTotal to push crypto-stealing malware
articles.summary: Cybercriminals are using a multi-platform campaign on GitHub, YouTube, and VirusTotal to distribute crypto-stealing malware disguised as legitimate trading and gambling tools. By manipulating platform metrics and feedback, the attackers successfully built a false sense of trust to deceive users.

articles.title: From Assistive to Agentic: The AI Shift That's Redefining Threat Management
articles.summary: The shift from assistive to agentic AI is being proposed as a solution to address enterprise security tool fatigue, data siloes, and slow incident response times. By automating triage, these AI agents aim to reduce analyst burnout and shorten breach dwell times.

articles.title: Microsoft: June 2026 Windows updates break Recycle Bin prompts
articles.summary: Microsoft has acknowledged a bug in the June 2026 Windows updates that displays incorrect filenames during the Recycle Bin file deletion confirmation process. The issue causes confusion for users but does not appear to pose a security threat.

articles.title: Britain's privacy watchdog quits after 'poor judgment' admission
articles.summary: The head of Britain's Information Commissioner's Office, John Edwards, has resigned following an internal investigation that revealed instances of poor judgment and inappropriate conduct. His departure creates a leadership vacancy at the top of the country's data privacy regulatory body.

articles.title: UK's information commissioner resigns over ‘inappropriate humour’
articles.summary: UK Information Commissioner John Edwards has resigned from his position following an investigation into allegations of inappropriate humor, which he ultimately deemed rendered his role untenable. His departure marks a significant leadership change for the UK's data protection regulator.

articles.title: Rights groups brand Home Office's AI age guesser for asylum-seekers as biased and inaccurate
articles.summary: Rights groups are criticizing the UK Home Office's implementation of AI-based age verification technology for asylum seekers, citing concerns over systemic bias and technical inaccuracy. Critics argue the tool cannot reliably differentiate between minors and adults at the critical age thresholds required for processing.

articles.title: Unauthenticated RCE in Splunk Enterprise under active attack (CVE-2026-20253)
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical, actively exploited unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in Splunk Enterprise (CVE-2026-20253) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, requiring immediate patching.

articles.title: Forget traffic lights, Google’s reCAPTCHA may ask for hand gestures
articles.summary: Google has introduced hand gesture verification as a new reCAPTCHA method within its Cloud Fraud Defense platform to better distinguish human users from automated bots. This feature adds an additional layer of challenge-based verification to prevent fraud and account abuse across various web forms.

articles.title: CISA: Splunk Enterprise flaw actively exploited, patch by Sunday
articles.summary: CISA has issued an emergency directive for federal agencies to patch a critical, actively exploited vulnerability in Splunk Enterprise by this Sunday. The mandate aims to mitigate ongoing attacks targeting the identified security flaw.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Splunk Enterprise flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and urges agencies to fix it by Sunday
articles.summary: CISA has added the critical CVE-2026-20253 authentication vulnerability in Splunk Enterprise to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating that federal agencies patch the flaw by Sunday.

articles.title: Forget Data Leakage: Shadow AI's Real Threat Is Access Control
articles.summary: The focus of enterprise security regarding Shadow AI is shifting from data leakage to the risks associated with unauthorized access control. Organizations must move beyond basic usage policies to address how AI tools gain access to sensitive internal systems.

articles.title: FIFA World Cup 2026: Hackers Target Football Fans With Fake Tickets Sites
articles.summary: Cybercriminals are launching phishing campaigns targeting FIFA World Cup 2026 fans through fraudulent ticket sites, fake hotel bookings, and malicious live chat features. These coordinated efforts aim to steal sensitive information and funds from unsuspecting event attendees.

articles.title: Mastodon 4.6 adds profile Collections and two-factor controls
articles.summary: Mastodon version 4.6 introduces new profile management features and empowers server administrators to mandate two-factor authentication for user accounts. This update enhances platform security and administrative oversight for instance operators.

articles.title: Google sets timeline for Android developer verification enforcement
articles.summary: Google has established a timeline for mandatory Android developer verification, beginning in select markets on September 30, 2026, before a global rollout in 2027 to enhance app security. The initiative requires developers on multiple major app stores to verify their identities to combat malicious app distribution.

articles.title: Accenture to buy Dragos, runZero, and NetRise in $4.2 billion cybersecurity deal
articles.summary: Accenture is acquiring stakes in Dragos, runZero, and NetRise for $4.2 billion to strengthen its end-to-end operational technology and critical infrastructure security capabilities.

articles.title: Salesforce Disables Klue App Integration After OAuth Token Abuse Exposes Customer Data
articles.summary: Salesforce has disabled the Klue Battlecards integration following a security incident that resulted in the unauthorized use of OAuth tokens to access customer data. The integration will remain suspended until further notice while the situation is addressed.

articles.title: NY man charged after harassing college student with AI-generated nudes
articles.summary: A New York man has been charged with cyberstalking for creating and distributing AI-generated non-consensual sexual imagery and fake messages to harass a college student. The case highlights the rising misuse of generative AI tools in targeted harassment and digital abuse.

articles.title: Peter Thiel ‘s Secret Society Leak Creates a Perfect Target List for Espionage, Influence Operations, and Blackmail
articles.summary: A website vulnerability in Peter Thiel's private Dialog network exposed sensitive member data, including political profiles and personal information. This breach poses significant risks for potential espionage, influence operations, and blackmail against the organization's high-profile members.

articles.title: BlackFog brings shadow AI visibility to macOS endpoints with ADX Vision
articles.summary: BlackFog has expanded its ADX Vision platform to macOS, enabling organizations to monitor and prevent unauthorized AI data usage across both Windows and Apple endpoints. This update aims to close security gaps by enforcing consistent AI data-loss policies to prevent sensitive information leakage via unsanctioned LLMs.

articles.title: CISA warns Fortinet users to secure devices after FortiBleed leak
articles.summary: CISA has issued an alert to Fortinet users to secure their devices following a significant data leak that exposed approximately 74,000 firewall and VPN credentials.

articles.title: Apple Patches Beats Studio Buds Flaw Letting Nearby Attackers Spy via Microphone
articles.summary: Apple has patched a high-severity vulnerability (CVE-2025-20701) in Beats Studio Buds that allowed unauthorized pairing and microphone eavesdropping via the Airoha Bluetooth audio SDK. Users are advised to update their devices to mitigate the risk of nearby attackers exploiting this flaw.

articles.title: Your browser tab could become encrypted storage for someone else’s files
articles.summary: Researchers have proposed Safecloud, a decentralized storage system designed to ensure user privacy by storing only encrypted data on nodes and separating encryption keys from data routing. This architecture aims to prevent storage nodes from accessing or reading the content of the files they host.

articles.title: 24 Billion Stolen Credentials Exposed in Massive Data Leak
articles.summary: Researchers discovered an exposed Elasticsearch cluster containing 24 billion records, including stolen credentials from infostealers and previous data breaches. The massive dataset poses a significant risk of large-scale account takeovers.

articles.title: Companies are discarding the logs they need to catch a breach
articles.summary: Large enterprises are intentionally discarding or failing to collect a significant portion of their log data to reduce operational costs. This practice critically hinders security teams' ability to detect and investigate potential data breaches.

articles.title: Asia-Pacific scam networks generate nearly $40 billion a year
articles.summary: INTERPOL's 2025/2026 report reveals that scam networks in the Asia-Pacific region generate nearly $40 billion annually, with cybercrime now accounting for over 30% of total recorded crimes in many jurisdictions. Rapid digital adoption is identified as a primary driver for this surge in regional cyber threats.

articles.title: New infosec products of the week: June 19, 2026
articles.summary: This article highlights new cybersecurity product releases for the week of June 19, 2026, including the launch of Fortinet's FortiSOC platform which integrates AI and SIEM/SOAR capabilities into a single SaaS solution.

articles.title: Gentlemen ransomware uses multiple EDR killers to disable defenses
articles.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service group is enhancing its attack capabilities by deploying multiple specialized tools designed to disable endpoint detection and response (EDR) software. This development allows their affiliates to bypass security defenses and remain undetected during operations.

articles.title: Authorities disrupt Evil Corp’s SocGholish botnet
articles.summary: Authorities and cybersecurity researchers dismantled the SocGholish botnet associated with Evil Corp by taking down 106 servers and cleaning 15,000 infected websites.

articles.title: Congress tees up No FAKES Act, aiming at AI-generated deepfakes
articles.summary: Congress has introduced the No FAKES Act, a bipartisan legislative effort aimed at protecting artists and performers from unauthorized, AI-generated deepfakes. The bill faces opposition from various business and digital rights organizations concerned about potential overreach.

articles.title: MacBook Neo vs Windows Laptops for Cybersecurity Tasks
articles.summary: This article explores the comparative advantages and limitations of MacBook and Windows laptops for cybersecurity professionals, focusing on tool compatibility and workflow efficiency.

articles.title: Bulgaria allowed surveillance tech firm to sell products to repressive regimes, report says
articles.summary: A Human Rights Watch investigation revealed that the Bulgarian government granted export licenses to the surveillance firm Circles, allowing the sale of intrusive technology to regimes with histories of human rights abuses. This highlights potential regulatory failures regarding the international trade of dual-use surveillance tools.

articles.title: Operation Endgame Disrupts SocGholish Malware Infrastructure
articles.summary: International law enforcement successfully dismantled the SocGholish malware infrastructure, seizing over 100 command-and-control servers and securing 15,000 compromised websites.

articles.title: Tor-Based Clipper Malware Targets Wallet Seed Phrases
articles.summary: A Tor-based clipper malware campaign discovered by Microsoft Threat Intelligence is actively targeting cryptocurrency users by hijacking clipboards, replacing wallet addresses, and stealing sensitive seed phrases. The malware also incorporates data exfiltration techniques such as taking screenshots from infected systems.

articles.title: Nintendo confirms data stolen in WebMD subsidiary cyberattack
articles.summary: Nintendo confirmed that personal survey data was stolen during a cyberattack on TinyPulse, a third-party service provider, though Nintendo's internal systems remained secure.

articles.title: F5 Patches Two Critical NGINX Open Source Flaws Enabling Remote Code Execution
articles.summary: F5 has released security updates to address two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX Open Source, including a use-after-free flaw in the HTTP/3 module. These patches are essential to prevent unauthenticated remote attackers from compromising affected systems.

articles.title: USB worm spreads crypto-stealing malware via Windows shortcut files
articles.summary: Threat actors are distributing self-spreading crypto-stealing malware that utilizes Windows shortcut files for infection and the Tor network for command-and-control obfuscation. The malware specifically targets cryptocurrency wallets by monitoring and intercepting clipboard data.

articles.title: Cisco fixed a critical ISE vulnerability that lets attackers to gain root access
articles.summary: Cisco has patched a critical command execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-20181, in its Identity Services Engine (ISE) that allows authenticated administrators to escalate privileges and gain root access.

articles.title: What Businesses Should Know Before Migrating Their CMS
articles.summary: The article outlines essential best practices for businesses transitioning to a new CMS, emphasizing the importance of data integrity, SEO preservation, and operational continuity. It highlights the necessity of meticulous planning, including audits and rollback strategies, to mitigate risks during the migration process.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: Claude Chat Abuse, NastyC2 npm Packages, Device-Code Phishing + 25 More Stories
articles.summary: This bulletin details a broad range of contemporary cyber threats including AI-based malware delivery, malicious npm packages, and sophisticated memory-only macOS attacks. It highlights how routine technologies are being exploited to facilitate phishing, credential theft, and cloud infrastructure compromise.

articles.title: How software development’s speed obsession enabled TeamPCP’s chaos crusade
articles.summary: The threat group TeamPCP has successfully exploited open-source software, highlighting how the industry's focus on rapid software deployment undermines security protocols. This trend suggests that current development cycles are creating avoidable vulnerabilities that threat actors are actively leveraging.

articles.title: Accenture shells out $4.18B on three companies in big industrial cybersecurity push
articles.summary: Accenture has invested $4.18 billion to acquire stakes in Dragos, runZero, and NetRise, marking a strategic expansion into operational technology security to address rising AI-driven threats. This acquisition spree signals a major focus on protecting critical infrastructure from advanced cyber threats.

articles.title: Google told researcher 'Nice catch!' Then denied bug bounty for flaw it still hasn't fixed
articles.summary: Google reportedly praised a security researcher for discovering a vulnerability but subsequently refused to pay a bounty, claiming the behavior was 'working as intended' despite the flaw remaining unpatched.

articles.title: Microsoft Details Windows Clipper Malware Campaign Using USB LNK Worm and Tor-Based C2
articles.summary: Microsoft identified a persistent cryptocurrency clipper campaign that utilizes USB LNK worms, Windows Script Host, and Tor-based command-and-control infrastructure to steal assets. The malware has been active since February 2026 and employs ActiveX logic to maintain persistence.

articles.title: Law enforcement hits SocGholish: 106 servers down, 15,000 sites cleaned
articles.summary: An international law enforcement coalition successfully dismantled 106 servers and remediated nearly 15,000 compromised websites associated with the SocGholish malware distribution operation. This action significantly disrupts the infrastructure used to deliver malicious fake software updates to victims.

articles.title: Australian sugar producer works to restore operations as ransomware group claims attack
articles.summary: Australian sugar producer Mackay Sugar has suspended harvesting and milling operations following a ransomware attack. The company is currently verifying claims made by a cybercriminal group regarding the incident.

articles.title: Klue OAuth breach linked to 'Icarus' Salesforce data theft attacks
articles.summary: Market intelligence firm Klue experienced an OAuth token breach exploited by the 'Icarus' threat actor group to exfiltrate sensitive Salesforce CRM data across multiple organizations. The attack is part of an ongoing extortion campaign targeting cloud-based information platforms.

articles.title: INC Ransomware Emerges as Major RaaS Threat in 2026 with 830+ Victims Since 2023
articles.summary: INC Ransomware has become a dominant RaaS operation, infecting over 830 victims since 2023 by absorbing affiliates from dismantled groups like LockBit and BlackCat.

articles.title: F5 Patches Critical NGINX Vulnerabilities Enabling Unauthenticated Code Execution
articles.summary: F5 has released emergency patches to address two critical, remotely exploitable memory corruption vulnerabilities in NGINX, identified as CVE-2026-42530 and CVE-2026-42055, which allow for unauthenticated code execution.

articles.title: The Scripts on Your Checkout Page Are Now a PCI DSS Problem
articles.summary: The updated PCI DSS standards now hold organizations accountable for third-party scripts running on their checkout pages, which pose significant security risks if compromised. Companies must implement monitoring solutions to ensure these external scripts comply with new regulatory requirements.

articles.title: 5 reasons Microsoft 365 backup isn’t enough for business data protection
articles.summary: This article explains that Microsoft 365's built-in features do not replace the need for dedicated third-party backup solutions to ensure comprehensive data protection and recovery. It highlights that businesses must proactively manage and secure their own data rather than relying solely on the provider.

articles.title: DragonForce Hackers Abuse Microsoft Teams Relays to Hide Backdoor.Turn C2 Traffic
articles.summary: DragonForce ransomware actors are utilizing a custom Go-based RAT called Backdoor.Turn to hide command-and-control traffic within Microsoft Teams relay infrastructure. This technique was identified during an attack on a major U.S. services firm.

articles.title: Police cleans nearly 15,000 SocGholish-infected sites tied to Evil Corp
articles.summary: International law enforcement successfully remediated approximately 15,000 WordPress sites infected by the SocGholish malware and neutralized over 100 servers associated with the Russian cybercrime group Evil Corp.

articles.title: ShapedPlugin update flow hacked to infect WordPress sites
articles.summary: Hackers compromised ShapedPlugin's update infrastructure to distribute malicious code to WordPress sites through legitimate plugin updates. This supply chain attack effectively turned a trusted vendor's delivery system into a vehicle for malware distribution.

articles.title: Malware attacks strip Roblox developers of entire games
articles.summary: Hackers are using malware to hijack entire Roblox games from developers, causing significant financial loss and limited recourse from platform support.

articles.title: eSentire links AI-led penetration testing with MDR through Atlas Preempt
articles.summary: eSentire has launched Atlas Preempt, an AI-driven offensive security tool that integrates continuous penetration testing data directly into its 24/7 Managed Detection and Response (MDR) services. The platform combines automated vulnerability discovery with human oversight to improve threat hunting and detection engineering.

articles.title: DragonForce Ransomware Abused Microsoft Teams to Hide Malware Activity
articles.summary: The DragonForce ransomware group leveraged Microsoft Teams relay systems to disguise a custom backdoor used to exfiltrate data and encrypt files at a US-based firm. This technique demonstrates a sophisticated use of trusted communication platforms to evade detection.

articles.title: Apple fixes Beats Studio Buds flaw that let hackers spy on conversations
articles.summary: Apple has issued a security patch for the Beats Studio Buds to address a high-severity Bluetooth vulnerability that allowed unauthorized individuals to eavesdrop on user conversations. The update mitigates the risk of remote spying for attackers within Bluetooth range.

articles.title: Telegram admits it couldn't police exam-leak channels, India tells court
articles.summary: The Indian government informed the Delhi High Court that Telegram acknowledged its inability to proactively detect channels distributing leaked exam materials, leading to a legal dispute over a platform ban. Telegram disputes the legality of the ban, asserting it has cooperated with authorities.

articles.title: 74,000 Fortinet firewall credentials exposed in FortiBleed data leak
articles.summary: A cybercriminal group inadvertently exposed a dataset containing credentials for nearly 74,000 Fortinet firewall and VPN gateway configuration files. The leak was discovered by a security researcher, prompting investigations into the compromised systems globally.

articles.title: Orphaned AI Agents: How to Find Hidden Access Risks Inside Your Network
articles.summary: The rapid adoption of autonomous AI agents has created significant security risks, specifically 'orphaned' agents with standing privileges that lack clear ownership or oversight. This administrative debt creates potential vectors for unauthorized access to core intellectual property.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes Windows Server 2016 security update failures
articles.summary: Microsoft has resolved a known issue that prevented June 2026 security updates from installing correctly on Windows Server 2016 systems. This fix ensures that devices not previously up to date can now successfully apply necessary security patches.

articles.title: Agentjacking: Researchers Show How One Fake Bug Report Can Hijack AI Coding Agents
articles.summary: Researchers discovered an 'Agentjacking' vulnerability where malicious bug reports can manipulate AI coding agents into executing unauthorized, harmful code. This risk highlights a new vector for compromising developer environments through automated software development tools.

articles.title: Microsoft Confirms RoguePlanet Zero-Day in Defender, Patch Under Development
articles.summary: Microsoft is developing a patch for the RoguePlanet zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-50656) in the Microsoft Defender Malware Protection Engine, which allows for privilege escalation. The flaw carries a CVSS score of 7.8.

articles.title: GentleKiller targets more than 400 security processes across 48 products
articles.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware gang provides their affiliates with specialized tools called GentleKiller to systematically disable endpoint detection and response (EDR) software. Internal data leaks have confirmed that these tools are designed to target over 400 security processes across 48 different products.

articles.title: Barracuda introduces AI-powered email security with automated threat response
articles.summary: Barracuda Networks has launched an AI-driven email security solution designed to automatically detect and remediate sophisticated threats within Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace environments. The platform integrates cross-domain telemetry to provide rapid response capabilities for managed service providers and organizations.

articles.title: New 42Crunch plugin helps developers find and fix API vulnerabilities in GitHub Copilot
articles.summary: 42Crunch has released a new plugin for GitHub Copilot that allows developers to identify and resolve API security vulnerabilities directly within their AI-assisted coding environment. This tool aims to help organizations secure their API infrastructure against increasing cyber threats.

articles.title: Blue Planet helps service providers reduce risk with unified network change governance
articles.summary: Blue Planet has launched Configuration and Change Management (CCM) software designed to mitigate operational risks by unifying network configuration and automating lifecycle management. The tool aims to reduce human error and system outages in complex, multi-vendor network environments through AI-driven workflows.

articles.title: FortiBleed Exposes Admin Passwords for 75,000 Fortinet Firewalls
articles.summary: Security researcher Bob Diachenko discovered an exposed server containing plaintext VPN credentials for 75,000 Fortinet firewalls, potentially impacting half of the internet-facing devices worldwide. The breach includes usernames, email addresses, and passwords for tens of thousands of organizations.

articles.title: Major US carrier stored credit card info in the clear, employee learned on first day
articles.summary: A major US telecommunications company was discovered storing customer credit card information in plaintext, a vulnerability that was identified by a new employee on their first day. The incident highlights the risks associated with improper data handling practices in the early 2000s.

articles.title: Welcome to your new telco job – here's sudo access to a database with full customer info stored in the clear
articles.summary: A major US telecommunications company in the early 2000s inadvertently granted a new employee unrestricted root-level access to a database containing sensitive customer information stored in plaintext.

articles.title: Securing digital keys when your phone unlocks the car
articles.summary: Alysia Johnson of the Car Connectivity Consortium discusses the evolution of the CCC Digital Key standard, highlighting advancements in interoperability, security, and credential management in Version 4. The interview addresses how cross-industry standards are being implemented to ensure secure digital vehicle access across various platforms.

articles.title: Google’s open standard for AI agents to discover and verify tools
articles.summary: Google has introduced Agentic Resource Discovery, an open specification designed to help AI agents locate, verify, and interoperate with tools across diverse platforms and organizations. This initiative aims to standardize how AI capabilities are shared in fragmented computing environments.

articles.title: How security teams are getting credential visibility into developer endpoints
articles.summary: Security teams are increasingly focusing on gaining visibility into developer endpoints to mitigate the risk of exposed credentials being exploited by supply chain attackers. This shift follows a series of widespread automated attacks targeting code repositories and package managers.

articles.title: Most agentic AI projects in production have stalled over data problems
articles.summary: Enterprises are experiencing stalls in agentic AI production deployments primarily due to significant challenges with data quality and governance. Despite increased adoption, these foundational data issues are hindering the transition of AI agents from experimental phases to fully operational production environments.

articles.title: Cyber offenses now account for around a third of all crime across Asia and South Pacific
articles.summary: Interpol reports that cyber-enabled crimes, particularly scams, now constitute approximately one-third of all criminal activity in the Asia-Pacific region. The findings highlight the growing challenge posed by AI-driven threats, especially for regions with limited financial resources for cybersecurity.

articles.title: Leak confirms OpenAI is testing a ChatGPT for Science subscription
articles.summary: Leaked information reveals that OpenAI is in the early stages of developing a specialized ChatGPT subscription tier tailored for scientific research and analysis. It remains uncertain whether this tool will be released to the general public or restricted to specific academic and professional entities.

articles.title: Google to use UK and EU user IP addresses for ad personalization
articles.summary: Google has announced plans to utilize IP addresses from UK, EEA, and Switzerland users for ad personalization and measurement starting in August 2026. This move highlights a shift in policy that faces scrutiny amid ongoing regulatory discussions regarding privacy and consent.

articles.title: Crypto Clipper Campaign Abuses Fake Reviews, AI Narrators, and VirusTotal Comments
articles.summary: An unknown threat actor is deploying a multi-channel campaign to distribute crypto-stealing malware by leveraging fake reviews, AI-generated content, and compromised or fake project pages on platforms like GitHub and SourceForge.

articles.title: Hostile states behind three-quarters of attacks on Britain's critical infrastructure, cyber chief warns
articles.summary: NCSC CEO Richard Horne reports that nation-state actors are responsible for 75% of attacks on UK critical infrastructure and are actively prepositioning for future conflicts. This highlights an increasing risk of sophisticated, state-sponsored cyber-espionage and sabotage.

articles.title: Microsoft Confirms RoguePlanet Defender Zero-Day, Says Patch is in Development
articles.summary: Microsoft is developing a patch for a privilege escalation zero-day vulnerability in the Microsoft Defender Malware Protection Engine, identified as CVE-2026-50656.

articles.title: Massive password-stealing attack hits 75k Fortinet firewalls
articles.summary: Approximately 75,000 Fortinet firewall devices have been targeted in a massive campaign designed to steal administrative credentials. Security experts urge immediate password rotation to mitigate the risk of unauthorized access.

articles.title: FortiBleed Attack Exposes Fortinet Firewall Credentials in 194 Countries
articles.summary: The FortiBleed campaign leveraged compromised credentials to gain unauthorized access to Fortinet firewalls across 194 countries, threatening the security of numerous public and private sector organizations.

articles.title: EU grants Ukraine access to cybersecurity reserve for major attacks
articles.summary: The European Union is granting Ukraine access to its specialized cybersecurity incident response reserve, further integrating the country into the bloc's collective defense framework. This initiative provides Kyiv with professional support to mitigate the impact of large-scale cyberattacks.

articles.title: Junior Hacker Used Tailscale and OpenSSH to Keep Access After His C2 Went Offline
articles.summary: A French-speaking attacker compromised a small automotive business and maintained persistence by installing OpenSSH and Tailscale on victim machines to bypass the reliance on a central command-and-control server.

articles.title: DragonForce Hid Inside Microsoft Teams and Nobody Noticed for Two Months
articles.summary: The DragonForce ransomware group successfully evaded detection for two months by utilizing Microsoft Teams infrastructure to route command-and-control traffic. By leveraging legitimate service relays, the attackers managed to mask malicious activity during an intrusion at a major U.S. services firm.

articles.title: Low-skilled attacker used Claude, Codex to breach 14 companies
articles.summary: OALABS researchers discovered that a low-skilled attacker successfully compromised 14 companies by leveraging AI coding assistants Claude and Codex to bypass safety guardrails. The findings confirm that AI-driven tools are effectively lowering the barrier to entry for conducting sophisticated offensive cyber operations.

articles.title: Attackers hit pair of critical Fortinet vulnerabilities the vendor disclosed in April
articles.summary: Multiple organizations are actively exploiting two critical vulnerabilities in FortiSandbox that were initially disclosed by Fortinet in April. The attacks are coming from various sources, indicating a widespread campaign rather than a single threat actor.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added the critical CVE-2026-48907 vulnerability affecting Widget Factory's Joomla Content Editor to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to evidence of active exploitation.

articles.title: FortiBleed leak exposes Fortinet VPN credentials for 73,000 devices.
articles.summary: The 'FortiBleed' data leak has compromised VPN credentials for nearly 74,000 Fortinet firewall devices globally. This incident poses a significant risk as it provides unauthorized access to enterprise network infrastructure.

articles.title: Digital sovereignty needs an operating model
articles.summary: The article explores the requirement for a structured operating model to achieve digital sovereignty in Europe, focusing on the region's goal to gain greater control over its technological ecosystem. It questions how these high-level political objectives can be translated into practical, sustainable operational frameworks.

articles.title: Another healthcare firm attacked days after Novo Nordisk breach
articles.summary: Medical technology firm iRhythm Holdings suffered a cyberattack leading to the theft of proprietary and patient-protected health information. The incident, disclosed shortly after a breach at Novo Nordisk, involves unauthorized access to third-party-hosted applications and an extortion demand.

articles.title: WitnessAI Agentic Control secures AI agents, tools, and MCP server access
articles.summary: WitnessAI has launched Agentic Control, a security platform designed to provide enterprises with centralized visibility and runtime governance over AI agents, tools, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server interactions. This solution aims to address security gaps as organizations increasingly deploy AI across development environments and internal workflows.

articles.title: Why Account Takeovers Are Rising and How to Stop Them
articles.summary: Account takeovers are increasing due to advanced tactics like MFA fatigue and session hijacking, prompting a shift toward device trust and continuous verification strategies. This article examines the current threat landscape and provides actionable defense recommendations to mitigate unauthorized access.

articles.title: Tigera introduces unified control plane for Kubernetes-based AI agent security
articles.summary: Tigera has launched Lynx, a unified control plane designed to manage, secure, and monitor AI agents within Kubernetes environments without requiring code modifications. The tool provides identity management, policy enforcement, and anomaly detection to address the unique security challenges posed by AI workloads.

articles.title: Cisco adds another SD-WAN box to max-severity bug advisory
articles.summary: Cisco has updated its security advisory for a maximum-severity vulnerability affecting additional SD-WAN hardware models. Administrators are urged to verify logs for signs of potential compromise even if patches have been applied.

articles.title: Homebrew 6.0 released with new security mechanism, Linux sandbox and more
articles.summary: Homebrew 6.0 has been released, introducing a new security mechanism and Linux sandboxing to improve the package manager's overall security posture. The update follows commentary from the project lead regarding the historical and current vulnerability landscape of package management systems.

articles.title: Rokarolla Android trojan targets banking and crypto users, enables device takeover
articles.summary: The Rokarolla Android banking trojan masquerades as legitimate applications to compromise 217 banking and crypto platforms, granting attackers full device control via accessibility services. Distributed through malicious websites, it poses a significant threat to user financial data and account security.

articles.title: India's Telegram ban hit the UAE too. Here's how to get around it
articles.summary: India's temporary ban on Telegram due to illegal exam paper leaks has caused widespread connectivity disruptions, allegedly exacerbated by BGP hijacking affecting users as far as the UAE. The article outlines the technical cause of the outage and suggests using MTProto proxies to bypass regional restrictions.

articles.title: SpyCloud Report Finds Phishing Attacks Surge as Employee Data Is Exposed at 86% of Fortune 100 Companies
articles.summary: A SpyCloud report reveals that 86% of Fortune 100 companies have suffered exposed employee data, directly contributing to an increase in phishing attacks. This underscores significant vulnerabilities in enterprise identity security.

articles.title: Flip expands platform with digital identity, no-code apps, and AI automation
articles.summary: Flip has introduced 'Frontline Identity' and 'Flip Fusion' to provide secure digital identity, application access, and AI-driven workflow automation specifically for frontline employees. These new tools aim to bridge the gap between mobile communication and enterprise-level system security.

articles.title: Corelight enhances Open NDR to detect AI-driven threats and unknown assets
articles.summary: Corelight has updated its Open NDR platform to improve asset visibility and threat detection, specifically addressing the rapid exploitation risks posed by AI-driven cyber threats. The enhancements integrate passive asset classification with its Zeek-based analysis engine to counter vulnerabilities that outpace traditional patching cycles.

articles.title: 152 Chrome Live Wallpaper Extensions Hid Ad Tracking and Fake Search Clicks
articles.summary: A discovery revealed that 152 Chrome wallpaper extensions were operating as malicious tools, secretly logging user data and generating fraudulent ad clicks. These extensions disguised their traffic to deceive users and ad networks while maintaining a legitimate-looking interface.

articles.title: Heimdal Survey: Executives Four Times More Confident About AI Risk Than the Teams Managing It
